title: Structured Meeting Facilitation with LLMs: From Summary to Action (2026)

questions.question: Meeting notes end as a flat bullet list with no owners or deadlines, and nothing happens. What structure fixes that?
options: Longer bullet lists
Fancier transcription bots
No notes at all, pure memory
Typed artifacts: decisions, owned actions, questions, parking lot
questions.explanation: Flat lists destroy accountability signals. This lesson types every artifact with its consumer and shelf life.

questions.question: How does classify handle 'This is out of scope for today; revisit next quarter.'?
options: Action, because revisit is an instruction for the team
ParkingLot, because the defer and next-quarter signals mark a future topic
Decision, because the meeting has resolved not to discuss it
OpenQuestion, because every deferred topic is unresolved
questions.explanation: The text has no earlier decision or action marker. 'Out of scope for today' and 'next quarter' match the parking-lot patterns, so the item is deferred rather than published as an action.

questions.question: What does score_action report for the sample 'Security review' owned by 'the team' with deadline 'asap' and DoD 'done'?
options: PASS, because a security review is important enough to publish immediately
3/4, because only the owner is too vague
BLOCK with score 0/4, because the description, owner, deadline, and DoD all fail
CONDITIONAL, because vague deadlines are accepted when the team is named
questions.explanation: The noun phrase has no qualifying verb or length, 'the team' is not a single owner, 'asap' is vague, and 'done' is too short. All four rubric fields fail.

questions.question: What score does the Kafka ADR action receive when the description, deadline, and DoD pass but two people are listed as owners?
options: 0/4, because any multiple-owner item is discarded
2/4, because the description and deadline are the only fields that matter
4/4, because two named owners are stronger than one
3/4, because only the single_owner field fails
questions.explanation: The description is long and verb-led, the date is specific, and the DoD has enough detail. The comma-separated owners fail only the single-owner check, producing 3/4 and a blocked report.

questions.question: Which type does classify return for 'Do we know if the legal team has reviewed the DPA?'?
options: OpenQuestion, because 'Do we know' is an open-question signal
Decision, because the DPA is a governance topic
Action, because the legal team must review it
ParkingLot, because no deadline is present
questions.explanation: The sentence has no decision or action marker, and 'Do we know' matches the open-question patterns. The classifier preserves that uncertainty for follow-up.

questions.question: What is the safe default for a raw meeting item that matches none of the classifier's signal patterns?
options: Decision, so the meeting record never loses a commitment
ParkingLot, so an unclassifiable note cannot silently become an action or decision
Action, assigned to the meeting facilitator automatically
OpenQuestion, because every unmatched note is a question
questions.explanation: classify defaults to ParkingLot. That conservative choice keeps ambiguous text out of the published decision and action artifacts until a person can interpret it.
